deposits.notes:
The paper and screening form both name https://osf.io/9ckra/; found_by is paper. The public OSF node has the earlier title "A double-edged sword in creativity: How LLMs influence individual creativity through dual opposing pathways". The node API explicitly reports public=true and anonymous read permission.

The landing page, node metadata, storage-provider listing, osfstorage root, both experiment folders, children, and wikis endpoints all returned HTTP 200. Root listing: https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/9ckra/files/osfstorage/ (two folders, Exp1 and Exp2). Children: https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/9ckra/children/ (zero). The only storage provider is osfstorage; there are zero wikis. Each folder lists five files; no further pages. Exactly ten files are listed, all XLSX; no analysis code, README/codebook, preregistration, or separate supplementary document is in this deposit.

All ten workbooks were downloaded without credentials using urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and inspected with openpyxl in memory. Each is below 20 MB. Downloaded byte counts and SHA-256 hashes match the OSF metadata for all ten files. Exp1_fixation_rating.xlsx is version 2; the other workbooks are version 1. Initial short OSF download links for Exp1_idea.xlsx and Exp2_survey.xlsx timed out before a response status could be confirmed; the OSF file-service URLs below succeeded with HTTP 200.

rows_checked=408 is the sum of 204 participant analysis rows in each model workbook, not a claim that the studies contain 408 different people. Each model has 204 unique IDs and complete assignment, CF, IS, and C values. columns_checked is the union of nonblank original headers across all ten workbooks; trailing header spaces and the distinct Rating1/Rating 1 spellings are preserved.

Assignment coding is identified by matching the participant prefixes, room/task text, and model-file creativity cell means to the eight means printed on pp. 5 and 7; no separate codebook is supplied. S1: PT=0 is human partner (HH IDs), PT=1 is LLM partner (HAI IDs). S2: NC=0 is batch-responsive LLM (NAI IDs), NC=1 is constrained-responsive LLM (CAI IDs). Both studies: TC=0 is the tire-use task and TC=1 is the VR-glasses task. The observed analyzed cell counts are S1 human/simple=50, human/complex=50, LLM/simple=52, LLM/complex=52; S2 batch/simple=50, batch/complex=50, constrained/simple=52, constrained/complex=52. These are counts of posted analysis rows; a separate randomized enrollment/attrition roster was not found.

C is participant-level creativity and CF is participant-level creative fixation: averaging the two idea-level ratings within participants reproduces all S1 C and CF values and all S2 CF values, with the one S2 C discrepancy below. IS is the model-file inspiration measure; the survey files also contain IS1-IS5, self-reported creativity, demographics, and manipulation checks.

The idea files contain 1,093 S1 and 1,204 S2 Chinese participant outputs, each with user_name, created_at, and room_name. Both idea files and all four rating files cover every model ID after normalizing complex-task IDs from (C)HAI01 to HAI01C, for example. Normalize Unicode width with NFKC for survey IDs: the S2 survey uses a fullwidth opening parenthesis in complex-task IDs. S2 survey then has a complete one-to-one match to all 204 model IDs. The participant texts support per-person and within-arm/between-arm diversity measures. The fixation workbooks additionally contain interleaved partner ideas; partner rows are not participant outputs and should be filtered accordingly.

Data-quality issue 1: Exp1_survey.xlsx has 204 participant-ID rows but only 203 distinct normalized IDs. Excel rows 90 and 91 both contain (C)HH39, with different responses; HH40C is absent. Do not silently relabel or merge these rows. This affects joining those survey responses to individual outcomes, but the S1 model, idea, and rating files have all 204 distinct IDs.

Data-quality issue 2: Exp2_model.xlsx, Sheet1, row 82 gives NAI31C C=2.07142857142857. In Exp2_creativity_rating.xlsx, Sheet1, rows 449-462 for (C)NAI31, 13 ideas have ratings 2 and 2 and one has ratings 3 and 2; their participant average is 2.0357142857142856. This is the only participant creativity mean that does not reproduce its model-file value. No correction or choice between these two sources has been inferred.

OSF node_license is null and no licensing file is listed. The article states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, but that does not establish a licence for these separately deposited data.

what_we_could_compute: S1 and S2, final.open_items questions 2 and 9: participant-level means across rated ideas, and arm-specific means, sample SDs, SEs, analyzed counts, and pooled/task-specific comparisons for expert-rated creativity (C) and creative fixation (CF). The model tables already contain the participant averages, and the output-level files contain both raters. These data allow the printed cell dispersion labels to be checked. The single S2 model-versus-rating discrepancy must be reported or resolved before selecting a definitive estimate.

S1 and S2, questions 5 and 9: analyzed counts for each of the four cells and the pooled partner/response-type arms can be counted directly. The files do not independently establish all randomized enrollment counts, exclusions, or attrition.

S1, questions 1 and 3: re-estimate the two-by-two creativity ANOVA and task-specific contrasts, and compute raw-difference and standardized-effect confidence intervals to audit the printed inconsistencies. Data cannot prove which confidence-interval estimand the authors intended to print.

S2, question 4: CF, IS, C, NC, and TC supply the participant-level variables for re-estimating the moderated mediation analysis. The exact original analysis specification and the intended published index still require verification; there is no deposited analysis code.

S2, question 10: after normalizing ID formatting, join all 204 survey rows to the model table and recompute arm means, SDs, SEs, counts, and comparisons for self-reported creativity. S1 individual-level survey joins require resolving the duplicated HH39C/missing HH40C ID.

Both studies: join participant idea texts to arm and task assignments to calculate per-person idea counts and within-person, within-arm, or between-arm diversity/homogenization measures. Restrict to participant outputs; the separate partner-text rows are not independent participant responses.
notes:
The entire 60,226-character markdown conversion was read, including the references and all end matter, for the saved 10-page version of record. There is no appendix in this PDF. Relevant statements and locators were checked against PyMuPDF page text, including the data statement on p. 9 and additional information on p. 10. Quotes are extracted verbatim from the supplied markdown; typographic line wrapping in URLs is retained. No separate code-availability or preregistration statement was found.

Public participant-level data, assignment indicators, expert outcome scores, and original ideas are directly verified for both randomized studies. Confidence is high for data availability; it does not imply the files are free of errors. The two data discrepancies are documented in the OSF notes. Do not infer cross-study person overlap from the distinct pseudonym formats.

The DataCite, Zenodo, Harvard Dataverse, and specified OSF nodes APIs were searched by the published title and first-author name, then by the different title used by the known OSF project. Counts are the API totals, including versioned records where returned. All returned candidate titles were inspected; no additional relevant deposit was found. Failed attempts are recorded with n_results=null and successful retries separately.

All data/material destinations in the paper and the form data_and_code were checked. The form code_url is empty. The additional article licence link http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/ returned HTTP 200 and redirected to HTTPS. Publisher supplementary contents remain unchecked because of the bot challenge. The two deposits entries consist of one confirmed OSF deposit and the unresolved publisher supplementary destination.

Open questions about the intended published confidence intervals and mediation index, randomization-versus-analysis counts, precise instructions to fixation raters, messaging functionality, and participant overlap are not automatically settled by public data. Supplementary Section S5 and Tables S5-S8 were not accessible. No accounts were used, authors were not contacted, and no downloaded data were saved to disk.

Other HTTP links in the PDF were checked for completeness; these are cited literature, publisher permissions, or article metadata, not deposits for c043.
